appearance_wet: Typical of ripe pu-erh: soft, dark brown leaf.

description:
Yue Chen Yue Xiang is a Dayi product listed among the brand's ranges. The name, 'the older, the more fragrant', is also the most common slogan in all of pu-erh, which makes this tea hard to search for and easy to confuse with general sales talk.

Its recipe and leaf grade are not publicly set out. Assume only what is typical of its class: Yunnan large-leaf tea, wet-piled and pressed.

Brew it like other ripe Menghai tea, with a quick rinse, water near the boil and short early steeps.

When buying, make sure the listing means this Dayi product and not just the slogan. Chinese tea drinkers themselves argue about how far the saying holds, and ageing depends heavily on storage and starting material.
history: Little is documented about when this tea first appeared or how it has changed. It appears in Chinese buyer guides among Dayi's product names, but no first release year can be confirmed.
